Field Worlds

The observed world (the first two shops unlocked by day 6) is reconstructed from replay data. Controlled experiments show that the draw is state-dependent: seed and day initialize the random stream, while farm occupancy changes which random value is used for the shop. "World" here specifically means the day-6 snapshot (the 1st and 2nd shop combined) — the granularity every real agent's strategy studied so far has actually committed to. It isn't the only one possible: shops keep unlocking every 3 days through day 24, so a finer world defined on more of them is equally real, just not what a strategy has used yet. This page pools it across every replay this project has downloaded or generated: several studied agents' own folders, every top-player archive, and the 5-day "Daily Top-10" sweep — one dataset, filterable by source below.

World frequency — all 64 possible worlds on day 6

First shop — the 8 possible early worlds

The 1st shop always unlocks at step 72 (day 3.0) — a fixed, agent-independent moment 3 days before the 2nd shop (the "world" above) reveals. Only 8 possible values instead of 64, so a pattern here is easier to spot: does anything change already, this early, depending on which single shop just opened?

Probability shape

One pie per shop reveal (a new one unlocks every 3 days until all 8 are out by day 24), each showing that day's 8 possible outcomes for the currently-selected sources. Toggle a single source above (a specific player, say) and watch these reshape — a real, persistent skew for one player against the pooled shape is the closest this page gets to spotting whether a specific player's draws look different from everyone else's, and a skew that only shows up on, say, day 15 and nowhere else would stand out here too. The 64-way "world" (days 3+6 combined) already has its own table above with exact counts per pair — a pie over 64 slices mostly draws one giant "everything else" wedge and hides the signal these 8-slice ones show clearly, so it isn't duplicated here.
